author: Ehero7
quote:
Like every Nintendo game, Welcome Tour is clearly packed with passion and attention to detail that people have come to expect with every Nintendo game, but is severely hampered by its own concept.

Many of the mini games are fun, and the game does complete what it sets out to do, which is educating people who buy on how the Switch 2 works. But this game is a $10 tech-demo that is very upfront in the fact it exists as a tech demo, which offers very little justification in its price point.

If we compare it to a different tech demo by Nintendo, Wii Sports, the differences it what Welcome Tour could have been and what it is are clear: Wii Sports was a tech demo that introduced people to the Wii's motion controls in a way that was accessible, charming, and endlessly replayable. Most of all, it was packaged with every early Wii sold, for free. Welcome Tour certainly has its charms, but is such a far cry away from what Nintendo was capable of. Wii Sports is a game that you'd expect to pay $10-$15 for, that's free; Switch 2 Welcome Tour is a "game" that you'd expect to be free, but pay $10 for.

author: Ehero7
quote:
ARMS is a very fun game, and leverages the fidelity of motion control given by the joy-cons to the fullest, generating a unique experience for a fighting game that is both fun and easy to play with people who are not as attuned to fighting games.

The game does feel a bit bearbones, however; just very short in terms of story and character depth, very akin to street fighter, but missing the character writing and lacking the room to develop characters that street fighter has fortunately seen by being a long series.

Overall, ARMS is a very fun game, and succeeds in core gameplay, but just leaves you wishing that there was a little bit more.

author: Ehero7
quote:
A phenomenal game, with phenomenal quality, that shows once again that ArcSys has struck gold with their development techniques. Dragon Ball FighterZ has so much attention to detail, and so expertly captures the artstyle and motion of the anime, that it feels as if you're watching an episode that you yourself control. 

It really is a cut-above every other anime game out there, its just that good. This is the kind of game that has me wishing ArcSys could get their hands on and make fighting games for so many more anime, because they really have produced a game that is genre-defining.

author: Ehero7
quote:
Cuphead is a one-of-a-kind game. It just oozes with passion, and the unique artstyle, soundtrack, and SFX make this whole game eye and ear candy.

The bosses are very difficult, but fun. Not for the faint of heart, and will certainly induce rage at one point or another, but remains fair by giving less-skilled players tools to make battles a little easier. Unfortunately plane sections of the game lack these kinds of features, which makes them far less forgiving to greener players than the other fights in the game.

author: Ehero7
quote:
A polished, fantastic game that is truly worthy of being a 3D Mario title.

This game has undoubtedly the best movement that I have ever experienced in a platformer. It draws from elements of every past 3D Mario title, and then further innovates with unique mechanics that build and synergize with Mario's core movement that players have come to know. 

The kingdoms in the game are beautifully designed, with highly attentive layouts that make traversing both accessible and fun. And unlike many games that suffer from preventing high-skill players from finding the limits of what is possible in the game, Odyssey rewards players who are able to utilize movement options to their fullest.

Hours of fun, Odyssey will keep you glued to your screen. A low skill floor and high ceiling makes this a game that anybody can enjoy, and is undoubtedly one of the most polished, and mechanically sound platformers of all time.

author: Ehero7
quote:
I want to like this game, I really do. It is essentially Minecraft on steroids: Much higher depth to crafting and tool progression, more advanced building, and filled with a ton of mechanics that adds layers of difficulty and complexity to the game.

But the difficulty curve at the start of the game is just way too high in my opinion. The game gives you very little grace, you will starve almost immediately, and really any hostile entity will chase you down and kill you, because your health just gets demolished early game by anything and everything. Ideally a game like this would have a super high floor and a lower ceiling. But even at the very start, if your world generation puts you in a bad spot, you're just done for. This doesn't even mention that you essentially have to study for this game in order to understand even the basic mechanics for survival.

A game filled with so much potential, depth, and clear care taken with developing, but suffers from a very high skill floor that will ultimately alienate a lot of players from the game.

author: Ehero7
quote: A game filled with charm and fantastic character writing. The game really draws you in with the quality of its characters and dialogue, and takes such an unusual concept for a game and translates it so well. Only gripe is that investigation phases latter on can begin to drag a little, but overall the game maintains a pace that keeps you drawn to the screen, with iconic characters that leaves you begging to hear more banter.

author: Ehero7
quote:
DO NOT BELIEVE THE HYPE.

GTA VI is an impressive feat of immersion and map-making, but unfortunately suffers from shortcomings in all other aspects.

Capped at 30fps, well below the standard that's to be expected for modern games, GTA VI often fails to meet even that, with performance issues often tanking the framerate to 20fps and below. Alongside that, the game comes with a slew of bugs throughout that one would not expect from a published title that has been in development for so long.

The story of VI drags at many points, and lacks much of the charm in both its plot and core characters that has come to be associated with the series. Furthermore, despite a 13-year gap between the release of GTA V and VI, the game fails to innovate and improve on the gameplay, sharing many of the same flaws that have been present in several of the series's past games. 

In truth, GTA VI is, at its core, a 6-7/10 game whose score is further bogged down by low performance standards, a failure to meet even those standards, and bugs that lower the quality of the game to below what's acceptable for a AAA developer that has had over a decade to produce the game. What may be worst of all however, is that GTA VI fundamentally lacks the elements and charm that have made the GTA series so beloved to so many people.

author: Ehero7
quote: A perfect remake for a groundbreaking game. Nintendo revitalized the original Ocarina of Time with a stylized artistic direction that captures the essence of the original 1998 game. The attention to detail throughout the game is astounding, full of references and details for even the most minute elements. Truly an upgrade from the original in design, graphics, gameplay, QOL features, and a slew of other elements, making it the definitive way to play one of the most influential games of all time.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
